resumen: Rahab told what they had heard in Jericho about the Lord and acknowledged that He is God in heaven and on earth. A letter about what we do with what we hear about God.

versos.texto: For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you, when you came out of Egypt; and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you utterly destroyed.
As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there wasn’t any more spirit in any man, because of you: for the LORD your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath.

reflexion: Rahab is still talking with the spies on the roof. Now she tells them what they had heard in Jericho. They had heard that the Lord dried up the water of the Red Sea when Israel came out of Egypt. And also what happened to Sihon and Og, the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan.

It is a hard passage, about war and destruction. We tell it as the Bible tells it, without dressing it up. The whole city heard the same news. And everyone's heart melted, Rahab's too. These are the words of Rahab, a woman of Jericho.

After telling what they had heard, she acknowledges that the Lord is God in heaven and on earth. In the verses that follow, Rahab asks the spies to deal kindly with her family. Maybe you too have heard about God many times. That can remain just noise, or it can reach your heart.

Today you can stop for a moment and ask yourself what you know about Him, and what you want to do with it. You don't need to know everything to begin to trust. Rahab acknowledged the Lord as she spoke of what she had heard about his works.
dedicatoria: This letter is for you, who have heard about God and still don't know what to do with it. You can begin today.
oracion: Lord, you are God in heaven and on earth. Thank you for what you tell us about yourself in your Word. May what we hear about you not remain just noise, but lead us to trust in you. In Jesus' name, amen.
